master.title: CHINA - Press Review [16 September]
master.content:
EU DELEGATION PRESS REVIEW - 16 September 2022

Political, Press & Information Section


EUROPEMembers of the European Parliament condemn China's exercises in Taiwan Strait

Members of the European Parliament on Thursday backed a resolution condemning China's live-fire military exercises in the Taiwan Strait and calling for closer ties between the EU and Taipei, Reuters reports. SCMP says that the bloc is under mounting pressure to begin modelling for the worst-case scenario in Taiwan - a mainland Chinese attack that would upend global supply chains. European diplomats were quoted as saying that fears of leaks to Beijing make it difficult to hold meetings on Taiwan.

Energy

China's financial news portal wallstreetcn thinks that the emergency intervention in Europe's energy markets might not effectively save the continent from its energy crisis, as a likely longer and colder winter might increase the demands for natural gas. European leaders may count on a more serious global warming to undermine their crisis, the report says.

Cankaoxiaoxi selectively translated an article by Hong Kong media Asia Times, which says that Europe is splitting over the Ukraine issue as energy crisis looms.

GT reports that whilst strikes roll across Europe due to the energy crisis and soaring inflation, the shale gas industry in the US warned that it could not save Europe by providing more oil and gas production as Biden had promised before, which is a clear indication that the US is not a reliable ally for Europe.

EU-China trade & investment

An FT opinion piece believes that cutting Germany's risky trade dependence on China and moving to diversify and rebalance Berlin's export-industrial complex would generate good outcomes. Yicai cites former Vice President of the European Chamber of Commerce in China (EUCCC) Stefan Sack as saying that the interdependence of Chinese and German businesses will hardly be broken in a short time.

SCMP reports that Dutch chip manufacturing tool maker ASML might further expand its workforce in China, where its employee headcount has tripled over the past five years. Japan Times points out that even as China loses its lustre, some European companies have poured in an extra 15% in investment in the first half of this year. Yet another SCMP article takes note of a Rhodium Group study, which shows that China's receipt of foreign direct investment (FDI) may not be as promising as its double-digit growth figures suggest, as the EU investments increasingly concentrated around a few large multinationals, certain sectors and countries, and virtually no new European firms have chosen to enter the Chinese market in recent years.

The Charge d'Affaires at the Chinese Embassy in Italy published via Italian media Agenzia Nova an op-ed entitled Prospects for China-Italy Cooperation on Belt and Road Initiative Remain Bright. The article has been picked up by People's Daily Online.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed a new legislation on Wednesday to reduce EU's dependence on supply of critical minerals from China. GT thinks that the move will increase the cost of achieving Europe's green targets and exacerbate its current economic woes amid the deepening energy crunch.

Other

Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh said at a summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) that he supports the construction of oil and gas pipelines from Russia to China via Mongolia, Reuters reports. Xinhua reveals that the three countries confirmed the extension of the Outline of the Development Plan on Establishing the China-Mongolia-Russia Economic Corridor by five years, officially launched the feasibility study on the upgrading and development of the central-route railway of the China-Mongolia-Russia Economic Corridor. However, a Beijing-based industry expert told Reuters that China might not need more Russia gas, and there is little support for Power of Siberia 2 to materialise before 2030. He also indicated that it would be a tremendously complex negotiation that could take years.

A researcher from the Institute of European Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences analyses on GT that since the traditional European political parties are unable to find good solutions for the ageing crisis, the fiscal problems, the refugee issue and the Ukraine crisis, European populism has been on the rise. The expert also warns that many populist politicians lack the experience to rule a country, and some of their remarks and policies are too extreme, therefore they could pose a huge political risk to the EU.

GT notes the meeting between the foreign ministers of France and India held on 14 September, during which the two leaders stressed their commitments to cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region, and expressed their shared concerns about China's rising influence in the region.

POLITICO reports that a Chinese government delegation has been refused permission by the House of Commons authorities to attend Queen Elizabeth's lying-in-state, opening a fresh diplomatic rift with Beijing.

 

CHINA                                              


On the front page:

People's Daily(domestic paper edition in CN):

Xi Jinping talks with President Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan (photo). Xi Jinping receives the Order of Friendship from President Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan (photo). Xi Jinping meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin (photo). Xi Jinping attends sixth meeting of Chinese, Russian and Mongolian heads of State (photo). Seeking Truth publishes an important article by Xi Jinping entitled "Socialism with Chinese characteristics must be adhered to and developed consistently".

People's Daily (overseas paper edition in CN):

The same as above.

Note: Xinhua yesterday announced the above article by Xi Jinping, saying that the article stresses that socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era is the fruit of the great social revolution led by the Communist Party and the continuation of the great social revolution led by the Party, and must be carried out consistently. To realise the Party's historical mission in the new era, the most fundamental thing is to hold high the great banner of Socialism with Chinese characteristics.

POLITICAL

Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit

WHB reports that the 22nd meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) was held in the historic city of Samarkand, Uzbekistan, from 15 to 16 September. IT was attended by the leaders of 15 countries, with a new round of expansion of the organisation being one of the main topics of the summit. The author comments that the growing influence of SCO is attracting more countries to join the organisation.

In Guancha, Pan Guang, Director of the SCO Research Centre at the Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences, Senior Advisor to the Middle East Society of China and Soft Science Expert at the National Counter-Terrorism Office, analyses SCO's potential role as mediator of the war in Ukraine, the pressures it is facing directly, and the forces of influence in the Central Asian region.

Putin-Xi Meeting

Bloomberg reports that Putin acknowledges Xi's questions and concerns about his invasion of Ukraine, a rare admission of tensions between the diplomatic allies and comments that the remarks at their latest meeting are the latest indication that Xi will continue to withhold material support as Putin suffers humiliating battlefield losses, and opposes any escalation that could further disrupt food and energy supply chains now roiling the global economy. Guardian also reports that Putin has told Xi that he understands China's questions and concerns about the war in Ukraine, in a rare nod to tensions between the two states caused by the Russian invasion. NYT reckons that China's support for Putin's war will become more shaky after the summit. FT also says that Russian president's comments are first public admission of differences between Beijing and Moscow. NYT says that Xi struck a far more subdued tone than the Russian president and steered clear in his public comments of any mention of Ukraine at all. Taken together, the remarks were a stark sign that Russia lacks the full backing of its most powerful international partner as it tries to recover from a humiliating rout in northeastern Ukraine last week. NYT observes that Mr. Xi did not repeat any of those lines from Chinese officials in his televised comments. He carefully avoided offering any endorsement of specific Russian policies, instead offering generalities about China's and Russia's view of the world. NYT also comments that the discordant messages of China's president, Xi Jinping, and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia suggested that despite an earlier pledge of friendship, Moscow does not have an unconditional ally in Beijing.

NikkeiAsia says that Beijing's account skips conflict and stresses support for respective core interests. NYT explains that Mr. Putin - who is also looking to close a deal on a critical pipeline that could allow Moscow to export more Siberian natural gas to China - most likely went into the meeting looking for something more substantial than a statement of ongoing support. But the issue of Ukraine is a fraught one for Beijing, analysts said. Providing additional help to Russia, either economically or militarily, risks running afoul of Western sanctions and imperilling China's economy. CaixinGlobal reports on the MFA readout (in English) and quotes that the two presidents also agreed to deepen practical cooperation in areas such as trade, agriculture and energy.

SCMPsays that the Chinese leader opened the door for deeper cooperation on economic matters and its columnist (SCMP) also comments that Xi welcomes a weakened Putin at SCO summit and has a delicate balancing act to play between Russia and the other Shanghai Cooperation Organisation member states in Central Asia, quite a few of which feel threatened by the Russian leader - especially after Ukraine - and are not unhappy about his latest military setbacks.

WP says that China has maintained a delicate balance on Russia's war against Ukraine, calling for peace while endorsing Russian complaints that NATO was to blame because of the alliance's expansion. Beijing has tried to lend moral support to Putin without outright backing the invasion or sending financial or military assistance that would incur secondary sanctions. It also comments that in Central Asia, where countries for years have had to navigate between two giant powers locked in quiet competition, a diminished Putin could give Beijing a chance to expand its footprint.

Global Times commentary says that Russian and Chinese heads of state meet to inject stability into a troubled world. Caixin's report on the meeting also mentions that China is ready to work with Russia to inject stability into a world in turmoil. Putin wished the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China a successful outcome and believed that under the leadership of President Xi Jinping, China's economic and social development will continue to make new achievements.

Other meetings

Xinhua reports that Xi attended the sixth meeting of Heads of State of China, Russia and Mongolia on Thursday afternoon and Xi underscored the strong impetus and resilience of the cooperation among the three countries. Extension of the Outline of the Development Plan on Establishing the China-Mongolia-Russia Economic Corridor by five years was confirmed and the feasibility study on the upgrading and development of the central-route railway of the China-Mongolia-Russia Economic Corridor officially launched. The three ocuntries agreed to actively push forward the project on the Mongolian section of the China-Russia natural gas pipeline.

Caixin reports that Xi Jinping met with Tajikistan's President Rahmon. Xi stressed that China is willing to strengthen practical cooperation with Tajikistan, expand imports of high-quality agricultural products, raise the scale and level of bilateral trade, promote cooperation in infrastructure, water conservancy, transport and other fields, explore cooperation in green technology, digital economy and artificial intelligence, and help Tajikistan improve its transit transport capacity. China is willing to strengthen cooperation with Central Asian countries, including Tajikistan, namely through the China+5 Central Asian countries mechanism, deepen cooperation in counter-terrorism and jointly maintain peace and tranquillity in the region.

ThePaper reports that a Consulate General of Kazakhstan is to be set up in Xi'an, a regional centre of foreign political contacts in the northwest of China. This is its fifth consulate. According to the official website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, on 14 September 2022 local time, the relevant departments of China and Kazakhstan signed a number of bilateral cooperation documents in the fields of trade and economy, connectivity, finance, water conservancy, press and media. The two sides decided to set up mutual consulates general in Xi'an and Aktobe.

Caixin reports that Xi Jinping received the Order of Friendship from the President of Uzbekistan. This is the first time that the Order of Friendship has been awarded since its inception. Also Xinhua. ThePaper examines Uzbekistan, host of the SCO summit, on how it becomes a medium power.

Xinhua reported briefly on other meetings between Xi Jinping and Central Asian countries, namely with Azerbaijani President Aliyev, noting the 30th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Azerbaijan (Xinhua); with Belarusian President Lukashenko, noting the upgrade the bilateral relationship to an all-weather comprehensive strategic partnership (Xinhua); with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov (Xinhua); and with the Turkmen president (Xinhua).

Taiwan

Caixin reports on FM spokesperson's reaction to the US' Taiwan Policy Act, saying that China will take all necessary measures depending on the progress and final outcome of the bill. Mao Ning said the bill in question is a serious violation of the commitments made by the United States to China on the Taiwan issue, violates the one-China principle and the three joint communiqués of China and the United States, interferes in China's internal affairs, violates international law and the basic norms of international relations, and sends a serious wrong signal to the separatist forces of Taiwan independence. China is firmly opposed to this and has made solemn representations to the United States. Ifeng runs a long article analysing that the Taiwan Policy Act of 2022 is based on the Taiwan Relations Act of 1979. The Act covers US economic and military support for Taiwan and gives Taiwan the status of a "major non-NATO ally" in total disregard of the One China principle, signalling that Taiwan may become the US' closest partner. Over the past decade, the use of the so-called China threat theory for political gain has become a bipartisan campaign tool in the US. According to a Chinese researcher, if the US follows this current path on Taiwan, it will likely revive the US-Taiwan military alliance, which is a direct challenge to the foundation of US-China relations, and the Chinese mainland is bound to respond more forcefully.

WHB reports that the Shanghai Institute of International Studies (SIIS) team recently held an online seminar to discuss recent trends in US-China relations, possible changes in the US one-China policy and other topics, and to offer advice on how to properly handle the Taiwan issue. On the same day, the SIIS team also released a research report on "China-US Signal Release and "Action-Reaction" around Taiwan", a joint effort with the United States Institute of Peace. The report identifies the need to find guidance in the Shanghai Communiqué to maintain peaceful coexistence between the two countries, and in particular to avoid confrontation on the Taiwan issue due to miscalculation.

Guancha translates Gregory Mitrovich's recent article in SCMP borrowing from Joseph Nye's theory of nuclear deterrence to analyse the international situation and calling for a rapprochement between China and the United States at a time of continuing tensions in the Taiwan Strait.

Other

Xinhuareports that the Permanent Mission of China to the United Nations and the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs jointly held the launch of the "Working Together for a Better Future - Progress Report on the Belt and Road Initiative in Support of the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development" on 14 September. In his keynote address, Zhang Jun, Permanent Representative of China to the United Nations, said that the Belt and Road Initiative is a contribution of Chinese wisdom and solutions to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda, which is highly compatible with the 2030 Agenda in terms of concepts, objectives and initiatives, and provides strong support and impetus for the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals. "One Belt, One Road" is a road of solidarity, a road of win-win cooperation and a road of hope.

According to CCTV military news, the Russian Defence Ministry has issued an update saying that the Russian and Chinese navies have embarked on a second joint cruise in Pacific waters.

Guancha publishes the translation of an article in Hindustan Times, analysing the reasons why India joined the three pillars of the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF): to ensure resilience and security of supply chains and reduce dependence on China; to promote the green economy and energy transition and to help India achieve the COP26 targets; to promote fair economy in order to combat corruption and non-transparent practices. However, as the trade pillar of the IPEF does not commit to easing market access, India will not join this section. India is still trying to whitewash the fact that the IPEF is essentially about creating a China-exclusion chain to contain China's development.

CaixinGlobal explains how corrupt officials hide their wealth overseas. The Criminal Law stipulates that state employees who have deposits overseas shall report them to authorities in accordance with state regulations. Any state employee with a "relatively large" overseas deposit who knowingly fails to report it is deemed guilty of concealing overseas savings and can face imprisonment or detention for a term not exceeding two years.

ECONOMY
RMB exchange rate

SCMP reports that China's offshore yuan breaches key level of 7 per US dollar for the first time since July 2020. The yuan traded in the offshore market weakened about 0.5 per cent to 7.009 against the US dollar. In the onshore exchange market, the yuan held at 6.9950 against the US dollar.

Caixin analyses that against the backdrop of a firm tightening of monetary policy by the Federal Reserve, an intensifying energy crisis in Europe and a slowdown in domestic economic recovery, the US dollar index has become an important factor dominating the RMB's movement recently, and the exchange rate has become detached from the actual supply and demand of the RMB.

Nikkei.Asia analyst believes PBoC's defensive tactics toward the exchange rate have kept the depreciation orderly have in fact worked. Without those tactics, rate differentials, recent trade-related developments, and the likely net flow of capital would have probably led to a mini-speculative run on the RMB, but now instead is an orderly break of the 7.00 level.

The Paper reports that spokeswoman at the State Administration of Foreign Exchange Wang Chunying said that China's foreign exchange market showed strong resilience, with a surplus in both bank balances and foreign-related payments. Market expectations remain stable and transactions in the foreign exchange market were conducted rationally and orderly. The net inflow of cross-border capital under trade in goods continued to be relatively high, and the inflow of foreign capital through direct investment and other channels was steady and increasing.

Banks asked to cut deposits' interest rates

Caixin Global reports that China's cabinet Thursday told financial institutions to further slash fees to small and medium-sized businesses to lower government-imposed costs and ease the burden on market entities. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and sole proprietors still face many difficulties in production and operation, the State Council said Thursday in a circular. It vowed to use reform and innovative methods to help market entities overcome difficulties.

Nikkei.Asia notes that this is the first time since 2015 that some of China's biggest state-run banks have cut deposit rates. It is an attempt to boost growth without risking runaway depreciation of the RMB. Tian Yun, a veteran economist, told GT on Thursday that trimming deposit interest rate may help boost consumer spending and investment in China, which will accelerate economic growth. He said that banks work as the market intermediary, and the change of deposit interest rate by the banks usually follows market demand. He also noted that the deposit interest rates could be raised as market demands for cash rise.

Caixin finds that five months after the establishment of a market-based adjustment mechanism for deposit rates, large state-owned banks have, for the first time, independently lowered their listed deposit rates without adjusting their benchmark rates. The move means benchmark rates are no longer necessary for changes in listed rates, the market based adjustment mechanism for deposit rates established in April will guide banks to adjust deposit rates in line with changes in market rates. China News analyst believes that the current cut in deposit rates by major state-owned reveals the effectiveness of the deposit rate reform. After large banks cut deposit rates, more banks are expected to follow. In general, the downward in China's market risk-free rates will be a long-term trend.

An expert told GT that the reduction of deposit interest rate is conducive to reducing the cost of bank liabilities and ensuring the stable growth of credit from the supply side. By reducing the debt cost of banks, the financing cost and debt repayment burden of real enterprises and residents will be reduced.  The reduction of deposit interest rate will lead to the reduction of deposit interest, which to a certain extent is also conducive to reducing residents' willingness to save, they will try expanding current consumption and investment or changing to other financial products.

Property sector

Reuters reports that shares of Chinese property developers rallied on Thursday on hopes that cities in the mainland will roll out more relaxation measures to boost the embattled sector. President Xi Jinping said in a closed-door meeting in late August that reasonable relaxation policies should be implemented as soon as possible to turn around the housing market. The four top-tier cities, Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Guangzhou, are, however, excluded from being asked to roll out more relaxation.

The Economist analyst believes that China's property crisis has not gone away but getting worse and in the short run officials have little choice but to undertake a bigger bail-out. Part of the problem is Xi's fixation with zero Covid. Another part is that the government's original plan did not resolve the conflicts between growth and financial prudence, and between citizens' needs and the incentives of crony officials and developers.

FT notes that China's local government financing vehicles are rushing to buy vast quantities of land with borrowed funds, bailing out cities and provinces struggling for cash after an exodus of debt-stricken private sector developers. Official data show LGFVs accounted for almost a quarter of land sales in the first half of this year, compared with 9 per cent in the same period a year ago. The ratio exceeded 50 per cent in some less-developed small cities.

FT analyses that the government has been reining in conglomerates that expanded overseas via takeovers. Deleveraging is a key policy goal. Beijing restricted large overseas investment sprees five years ago, especially in areas such as hotels, entertainment, real estate and sports clubs. These were areas where Fosun had been an active acquirer. Fosun entity's plan to cut holdings in this core asset looks like a financial and political mistake and Fosun should sell overseas trophy assets first.

CE says that, according to the website of the National Bureau of Statistics, the real estate development boom index (National Housing Boom Index) was 95.07 in August. CE also notes that from January to August 2022, China's investment in real estate development fell by 7.4%.

Chips industry

SCMP reports that a record number of semiconductor-related Chinese corporate entities have ceased to exist in the first eight months of the year, according to the latest data from a domestic business registry service, signalling the sputtering state of the country's chip self-sufficiency drive.

The anti-corruption storm surrounding the National Chip Fund continues and Caixin learned that on September 15, Ren Kai, vice president of Huaxin Investment Management Limited was taken away by the relevant departments for investigation.

Caixin analyses that the US Chip Act is a nightmare for the chip industry in Japan, Korea and Taiwan. US aims to surpass and defeat Japan's equipment and materials, Korea's storage, and China and Taiwan's high-end manufacturing. Reuters says that the Biden administration plans next month to broaden curbs on US shipments to China of semiconductors used for artificial intelligence and chip making tools.

US tighten up scrutiny over foreign investments

The Biden administration will intensify national security reviews of foreign investments in the U.S. that involve personal data and advanced technologies and the press sees it as a move against China. Bloomberg/Caixin Global says that the new criteria will apply to sectors including semiconductors, artificial intelligence, biotechnology and clean energy technologies. The move reflects growing concern in the White House and among Democrats and Republicans alike especially about China, which seeks to rapidly match and eventually surpass the U.S. in a variety of high-tech industries, including through investments in American companies. SCMP says that the move appears aimed at national security risks that the US sees in China. President's executive order sharpens focus of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States, which reviews business acquisitions for national security risks. NYT says that it is bound to heighten tensions with Beijing and reflects growing unease about China's ability to access the personal information that Americans hand over to mobile apps and other services.

Other

FT questions Xi's plan for economic independence. Analysts believe that China's industry, technology, energy and agriculture cannot stand-alone. China cannot afford to completely isolate itself from the world due to its export-oriented structure. As a result, Beijing is likely to adopt a hybrid approach depending on the industry. SCMP reports that China continues to step up its unconventional policy tools to keep the national economy churning while trying to mitigate the damage from its zero-Covid policy. Premier Li vowed to further expand investment to create more demand and lift confidence amid a slight fluctuation in China's economy as it recovers. Meanwhile, the control measures remain high on Beijing's agenda ahead of the 20th Party Congress. Appearance by Vice-Premier Sun Chunlan, in charge of China's virus-control measures, at special cabinet meeting brings hope of better coordination between virus control and growth objectives.

Guancha analyst believes that China is experiencing a green revolution. Western leaders fear that, just as fossil fuels were coerced by the Russian energy giant, they could be coerced by China in a future decarbonised world. Instead of worrying about China falling into coal dependency, the west is now worried that China will dominate the future of renewable energy.

SCMP reports that China's top weapons scientist says nuclear fusion power is 6 years away. Peng Xianjue unveils plans for combined fusion-fission reactor that could make China world's first to achieve the elusive viable energy source. No country has so far managed to build a facility that generates more power than it uses in the fission process.

GENERAL ISSUES
Covid-19

Sina notes that Tianjin Municipality will launch the citywide nucleic acid testing on September 16. Caixin says that Shenzhen epidemic situation gradually eases, some primary and secondary schools return to school. GT reports that while stressing that China's COVID-19 strategy is adjusting dynamically, Chinese observers said that China should stick to this strategy at the current stage yet it heeds WHO's COVID guidance.

GT reports that spokesperson of Beijing municipal government at a news conference on September 15 said that COVID-19 clusters in three schools have dropped significantly and the risk of community spread is generally under control. The prevention and control of imported cases remains the top priority in the capital. China News notes that Beijing added 2 new confirmed local cases in Chaoyang on September 15, both identified during quarantine.

Other

Nearly two dozen Chinese regions have experienced a double-digit percentage drop in births in 2022, Nikkei.Asia research shows, putting the country at risk of falling short of the 10 million mark for the full year for the first time since the Communist Party took control.

GT reports that the Minister of Ministry of Ecology told Thursday's press conference that to achieve carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality is to address outstanding problems of resource and environmental constraints and realize the sustainable development of the Chinese nation. Therefore, we are determined to achieve the goals.

He carefully avoided offering any endorsement of specific Russian policies, instead offering generalities about China's and Russia's view of the world. NYT also comments that the discordant messages of China's president, Xi Jinping, and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia suggested that despite an earlier pledge of friendship, Moscow does not have an unconditional ally in Beijing.

NikkeiAsia says that Beijing's account skips conflict and stresses support for respective core interests. NYT explains that Mr. Putin - who is also looking to close a deal on a critical pipeline that could allow Moscow to export more Siberian natural gas to China - most likely went into the meeting looking for something more substantial than a statement of ongoing support. But the issue of Ukraine is a fraught one for Beijing, analysts said. Providing additional help to Russia, either economically or militarily, risks running afoul of Western sanctions and imperilling China's economy. CaixinGlobal reports on the MFA readout (in English) and quotes that the two presidents also agreed to deepen practical cooperation in areas such as trade, agriculture and energy.

SCMPsays that the Chinese leader opened the door for deeper cooperation on economic matters and its columnist (SCMP) also comments that Xi welcomes a weakened Putin at SCO summit and has a delicate balancing act to play between Russia and the other Shanghai Cooperation Organisation member states in Central Asia, quite a few of which feel threatened by the Russian leader - especially after Ukraine - and are not unhappy about his latest military setbacks.

WP says that China has maintained a delicate balance on Russia's war against Ukraine, calling for peace while endorsing Russian complaints that NATO was to blame because of the alliance's expansion. Beijing has tried to lend moral support to Putin without outright backing the invasion or sending financial or military assistance that would incur secondary sanctions. It also comments that in Central Asia, where countries for years have had to navigate between two giant powers locked in quiet competition, a diminished Putin could give Beijing a chance to expand its footprint.

Global Times commentary says that Russian and Chinese heads of state meet to inject stability into a troubled world. Caixin's report on the meeting also mentions that China is ready to work with Russia to inject stability into a world in turmoil. Putin wished the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China a successful outcome and believed that under the leadership of President Xi Jinping, China's economic and social development will continue to make new achievements.

Other meetings

Xinhua reports that Xi attended the sixth meeting of Heads of State of China, Russia and Mongolia on Thursday afternoon and Xi underscored the strong impetus and resilience of the cooperation among the three countries. Extension of the Outline of the Development Plan on Establishing the China-Mongolia-Russia Economic Corridor by five years was confirmed and the feasibility study on the upgrading and development of the central-route railway of the China-Mongolia-Russia Economic Corridor officially launched. The three ocuntries agreed to actively push forward the project on the Mongolian section of the China-Russia natural gas pipeline.

Caixin reports that Xi Jinping met with Tajikistan's President Rahmon. Xi stressed that China is willing to strengthen practical cooperation with Tajikistan, expand imports of high-quality agricultural products, raise the scale and level of bilateral trade, promote cooperation in infrastructure, water conservancy, transport and other fields, explore cooperation in green technology, digital economy and artificial intelligence, and help Tajikistan improve its transit transport capacity. China is willing to strengthen cooperation with Central Asian countries, including Tajikistan, namely through the China+5 Central Asian countries mechanism, deepen cooperation in counter-terrorism and jointly maintain peace and tranquillity in the region.

ThePaper reports that a Consulate General of Kazakhstan is to be set up in Xi'an, a regional centre of foreign political contacts in the northwest of China. This is its fifth consulate. According to the official website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, on 14 September 2022 local time, the relevant departments of China and Kazakhstan signed a number of bilateral cooperation documents in the fields of trade and economy, connectivity, finance, water conservancy, press and media. The two sides decided to set up mutual consulates general in Xi'an and Aktobe.

Caixin reports that Xi Jinping received the Order of Friendship from the President of Uzbekistan. This is the first time that the Order of Friendship has been awarded since its inception. Also Xinhua. ThePaper examines Uzbekistan, host of the SCO summit, on how it becomes a medium power.

Xinhua reported briefly on other meetings between Xi Jinping and Central Asian countries, namely with Azerbaijani President Aliyev, noting the 30th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Azerbaijan (Xinhua); with Belarusian President Lukashenko, noting the upgrade the bilateral relationship to an all-weather comprehensive strategic partnership (Xinhua); with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov (Xinhua); and with the Turkmen president (Xinhua).

Taiwan

Caixin reports on FM spokesperson's reaction to the US' Taiwan Policy Act, saying that China will take all necessary measures depending on the progress and final outcome of the bill. Mao Ning said the bill in question is a serious violation of the commitments made by the United States to China on the Taiwan issue, violates the one-China principle and the three joint communiqués of China and the United States, interferes in China's internal affairs, violates international law and the basic norms of international relations, and sends a serious wrong signal to the separatist forces of Taiwan independence. China is firmly opposed to this and has made solemn representations to the United States. Ifeng runs a long article analysing that the Taiwan Policy Act of 2022 is based on the Taiwan Relations Act of 1979. The Act covers US economic and military support for Taiwan and gives Taiwan the status of a "major non-NATO ally" in total disregard of the One China principle, signalling that Taiwan may become the US' closest partner. Over the past decade, the use of the so-called China threat theory for political gain has become a bipartisan campaign tool in the US. According to a Chinese researcher, if the US follows this current path on Taiwan, it will likely revive the US-Taiwan military alliance, which is a direct challenge to the foundation of US-China relations, and the Chinese mainland is bound to respond more forcefully.

WHB reports that the Shanghai Institute of International Studies (SIIS) team recently held an online seminar to discuss recent trends in US-China relations, possible changes in the US one-China policy and other topics, and to offer advice on how to properly handle the Taiwan issue. On the same day, the SIIS team also released a research report on "China-US Signal Release and "Action-Reaction" around Taiwan", a joint effort with the United States Institute of Peace. The report identifies the need to find guidance in the Shanghai Communiqué to maintain peaceful coexistence between the two countries, and in particular to avoid confrontation on the Taiwan issue due to miscalculation.

Guancha translates Gregory Mitrovich's recent article in SCMP borrowing from Joseph Nye's theory of nuclear deterrence to analyse the international situation and calling for a rapprochement between China and the United States at a time of continuing tensions in the Taiwan Strait.

Other

Xinhuareports that the Permanent Mission of China to the United Nations and the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs jointly held the launch of the "Working Together for a Better Future - Progress Report on the Belt and Road Initiative in Support of the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development" on 14 September. In his keynote address, Zhang Jun, Permanent Representative of China to the United Nations, said that the Belt and Road Initiative is a contribution of Chinese wisdom and solutions to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda, which is highly compatible with the 2030 Agenda in terms of concepts, objectives and initiatives, and provides strong support and impetus for the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals. "One Belt, One Road" is a road of solidarity, a road of win-win cooperation and a road of hope.

According to CCTV military news, the Russian Defence Ministry has issued an update saying that the Russian and Chinese navies have embarked on a second joint cruise in Pacific waters.

Guancha publishes the translation of an article in Hindustan Times, analysing the reasons why India joined the three pillars of the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF): to ensure resilience and security of supply chains and reduce dependence on China; to promote the green economy and energy transition and to help India achieve the COP26 targets; to promote fair economy in order to combat corruption and non-transparent practices. However, as the trade pillar of the IPEF does not commit to easing market access, India will not join this section. India is still trying to whitewash the fact that the IPEF is essentially about creating a China-exclusion chain to contain China's development.

CaixinGlobal explains how corrupt officials hide their wealth overseas. The Criminal Law stipulates that state employees who have deposits overseas shall report them to authorities in accordance with state regulations. Any state employee with a "relatively large" overseas deposit who knowingly fails to report it is deemed guilty of concealing overseas savings and can face imprisonment or detention for a term not exceeding two years.

ECONOMY
RMB exchange rate

SCMP reports that China's offshore yuan breaches key level of 7 per US dollar for the first time since July 2020. The yuan traded in the offshore market weakened about 0.5 per cent to 7.009 against the US dollar. In the onshore exchange market, the yuan held at 6.9950 against the US dollar.

Caixin analyses that against the backdrop of a firm tightening of monetary policy by the Federal Reserve, an intensifying energy crisis in Europe and a slowdown in domestic economic recovery, the US dollar index has become an important factor dominating the RMB's movement recently, and the exchange rate has become detached from the actual supply and demand of the RMB.

Nikkei.Asia analyst believes PBoC's defensive tactics toward the exchange rate have kept the depreciation orderly have in fact worked. Without those tactics, rate differentials, recent trade-related developments, and the likely net flow of capital would have probably led to a mini-speculative run on the RMB, but now instead is an orderly break of the 7.00 level.

The Paper reports that spokeswoman at the State Administration of Foreign Exchange Wang Chunying said that China's foreign exchange market showed strong resilience, with a surplus in both bank balances and foreign-related payments. Market expectations remain stable and transactions in the foreign exchange market were conducted rationally and orderly. The net inflow of cross-border capital under trade in goods continued to be relatively high, and the inflow of foreign capital through direct investment and other channels was steady and increasing.

Banks asked to cut deposits' interest rates

Caixin Global reports that China's cabinet Thursday told financial institutions to further slash fees to small and medium-sized businesses to lower government-imposed costs and ease the burden on market entities. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and sole proprietors still face many difficulties in production and operation, the State Council said Thursday in a circular. It vowed to use reform and innovative methods to help market entities overcome difficulties.

Nikkei.Asia notes that this is the first time since 2015 that some of China's biggest state-run banks have cut deposit rates. It is an attempt to boost growth without risking runaway depreciation of the RMB. Tian Yun, a veteran economist, told GT on Thursday that trimming deposit interest rate may help boost consumer spending and investment in China, which will accelerate economic growth. He said that banks work as the market intermediary, and the change of deposit interest rate by the banks usually follows market demand. He also noted that the deposit interest rates could be raised as market demands for cash rise.

Caixin finds that five months after the establishment of a market-based adjustment mechanism for deposit rates, large state-owned banks have, for the first time, independently lowered their listed deposit rates without adjusting their benchmark rates. The move means benchmark rates are no longer necessary for changes in listed rates, the market based adjustment mechanism for deposit rates established in April will guide banks to adjust deposit rates in line with changes in market rates. China News analyst believes that the current cut in deposit rates by major state-owned reveals the effectiveness of the deposit rate reform. After large banks cut deposit rates, more banks are expected to follow. In general, the downward in China's market risk-free rates will be a long-term trend.

An expert told GT that the reduction of deposit interest rate is conducive to reducing the cost of bank liabilities and ensuring the stable growth of credit from the supply side. By reducing the debt cost of banks, the financing cost and debt repayment burden of real enterprises and residents will be reduced.  The reduction of deposit interest rate will lead to the reduction of deposit interest, which to a certain extent is also conducive to reducing residents' willingness to save, they will try expanding current consumption and investment or changing to other financial products.

Property sector

Reuters reports that shares of Chinese property developers rallied on Thursday on hopes that cities in the mainland will roll out more relaxation measures to boost the embattled sector. President Xi Jinping said in a closed-door meeting in late August that reasonable relaxation policies should be implemented as soon as possible to turn around the housing market. The four top-tier cities, Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Guangzhou, are, however, excluded from being asked to roll out more relaxation.

The Economist analyst believes that China's property crisis has not gone away but getting worse and in the short run officials have little choice but to undertake a bigger bail-out. Part of the problem is Xi's fixation with zero Covid. Another part is that the government's original plan did not resolve the conflicts between growth and financial prudence, and between citizens' needs and the incentives of crony officials and developers.

FT notes that China's local government financing vehicles are rushing to buy vast quantities of land with borrowed funds, bailing out cities and provinces struggling for cash after an exodus of debt-stricken private sector developers. Official data show LGFVs accounted for almost a quarter of land sales in the first half of this year, compared with 9 per cent in the same period a year ago. The ratio exceeded 50 per cent in some less-developed small cities.

FT analyses that the government has been reining in conglomerates that expanded overseas via takeovers. Deleveraging is a key policy goal. Beijing restricted large overseas investment sprees five years ago, especially in areas such as hotels, entertainment, real estate and sports clubs. These were areas where Fosun had been an active acquirer. Fosun entity's plan to cut holdings in this core asset looks like a financial and political mistake and Fosun should sell overseas trophy assets first.

CE says that, according to the website of the National Bureau of Statistics, the real estate development boom index (National Housing Boom Index) was 95.07 in August. CE also notes that from January to August 2022, China's investment in real estate development fell by 7.4%.

Chips industry

SCMP reports that a record number of semiconductor-related Chinese corporate entities have ceased to exist in the first eight months of the year, according to the latest data from a domestic business registry service, signalling the sputtering state of the country's chip self-sufficiency drive.

The anti-corruption storm surrounding the National Chip Fund continues and Caixin learned that on September 15, Ren Kai, vice president of Huaxin Investment Management Limited was taken away by the relevant departments for investigation.

Caixin analyses that the US Chip Act is a nightmare for the chip industry in Japan, Korea and Taiwan. US aims to surpass and defeat Japan's equipment and materials, Korea's storage, and China and Taiwan's high-end manufacturing. Reuters says that the Biden administration plans next month to broaden curbs on US shipments to China of semiconductors used for artificial intelligence and chip making tools.

US tighten up scrutiny over foreign investments

The Biden administration will intensify national security reviews of foreign investments in the U.S. that involve personal data and advanced technologies and the press sees it as a move against China. Bloomberg/Caixin Global says that the new criteria will apply to sectors including semiconductors, artificial intelligence, biotechnology and clean energy technologies. The move reflects growing concern in the White House and among Democrats and Republicans alike especially about China, which seeks to rapidly match and eventually surpass the U.S. in a variety of high-tech industries, including through investments in American companies. SCMP says that the move appears aimed at national security risks that the US sees in China. President's executive order sharpens focus of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States, which reviews business acquisitions for national security risks. NYT says that it is bound to heighten tensions with Beijing and reflects growing unease about China's ability to access the personal information that Americans hand over to mobile apps and other services.

Other

FT questions Xi's plan for economic independence. Analysts believe that China's industry, technology, energy and agriculture cannot stand-alone. China cannot afford to completely isolate itself from the world due to its export-oriented structure. As a result, Beijing is likely to adopt a hybrid approach depending on the industry. SCMP reports that China continues to step up its unconventional policy tools to keep the national economy churning while trying to mitigate the damage from its zero-Covid policy. Premier Li vowed to further expand investment to create more demand and lift confidence amid a slight fluctuation in China's economy as it recovers. Meanwhile, the control measures remain high on Beijing's agenda ahead of the 20th Party Congress. Appearance by Vice-Premier Sun Chunlan, in charge of China's virus-control measures, at special cabinet meeting brings hope of better coordination between virus control and growth objectives.

Guancha analyst believes that China is experiencing a green revolution. Western leaders fear that, just as fossil fuels were coerced by the Russian energy giant, they could be coerced by China in a future decarbonised world. Instead of worrying about China falling into coal dependency, the west is now worried that China will dominate the future of renewable energy.

SCMP reports that China's top weapons scientist says nuclear fusion power is 6 years away. Peng Xianjue unveils plans for combined fusion-fission reactor that could make China world's first to achieve the elusive viable energy source. No country has so far managed to build a facility that generates more power than it uses in the fission process.

GENERAL ISSUES
Covid-19

Sina notes that Tianjin Municipality will launch the citywide nucleic acid testing on September 16. Caixin says that Shenzhen epidemic situation gradually eases, some primary and secondary schools return to school. GT reports that while stressing that China's COVID-19 strategy is adjusting dynamically, Chinese observers said that China should stick to this strategy at the current stage yet it heeds WHO's COVID guidance.

GT reports that spokesperson of Beijing municipal government at a news conference on September 15 said that COVID-19 clusters in three schools have dropped significantly and the risk of community spread is generally under control. The prevention and control of imported cases remains the top priority in the capital. China News notes that Beijing added 2 new confirmed local cases in Chaoyang on September 15, both identified during quarantine.

Other

Nearly two dozen Chinese regions have experienced a double-digit percentage drop in births in 2022, Nikkei.Asia research shows, putting the country at risk of falling short of the 10 million mark for the full year for the first time since the Communist Party took control.

GT reports that the Minister of Ministry of Ecology told Thursday's press conference that to achieve carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality is to address outstanding problems of resource and environmental constraints and realize the sustainable development of the Chinese nation. Therefore, we are determined to achieve the goals.
